speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the 3-minute duration and rapid resolution are key features. Given your age and sudden onset without hearing loss, have you noticed any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your limbs or face? REQUEST TEST: Dix-Hallpike Maneuver

text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The Dix-Hallpike maneuver was positive, reproducing your vertigo and nystagmus, which confirms this diagnosis given your brief, sudden episodes. I will now request images of your inner ear to document the specific canal involvement, though treatment will likely involve repositioning maneuvers.
